evidence.claim: Trong said Vietnam's foreign policy is one of independence, self-reliance, peace, cooperation and development, and diversification and multilateralization, while asking the new US ambassador to continue contributing to bilateral ties.
evidence.title: Party leader applauds progress in Vietnam - US relations
evidence.excerpt: Trong said Vietnam's foreign policy is one of independence, self-reliance, peace, cooperation and development, and diversification and multilateralization, while asking the new US ambassador to continue contributing to bilateral ties.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of a Trọng meeting with a foreign ambassador on Vietnam's external policy line.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Trọng; this is his own framing of foreign policy priorities and bilateral conduct.
contrary_evidence: This is broad diplomatic language, not a concrete crisis decision or armed-security operation.

evidence.claim: Trong said Vietnam considers the United Nations an important international partner and cooperation with the UN a foreign-policy priority, while praising the UN's role in peace, security and development cooperation.
evidence.title: Vietnam views United Nations as important international partner: Party chief
evidence.excerpt: Trong said Vietnam considers the United Nations an important international partner and cooperation with the UN a foreign-policy priority, while praising the UN's role in peace, security and development cooperation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of Trọng's remarks to the UN Secretary-General.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Trọng; it is his own statement on international institutions and peace-oriented cooperation.
contrary_evidence: This is institutional diplomacy, not evidence of a specific peace settlement or military restraint choice.

evidence.claim: Vietnam called on parties to exercise self-restraint, enhance dialogue, and peacefully settle differences in line with the UN Charter and international law, while saying it would protect Vietnamese citizens in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Viet Nam calls on relevant parties in Ukraine crisis to exercise self-restraint
evidence.excerpt: Vietnam called on parties to exercise self-restraint, enhance dialogue, and peacefully settle differences in line with the UN Charter and international law, while saying it would protect Vietnamese citizens in Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government statement issued on the day of Russia's full-scale invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect to Trọng through party-state leadership; this is the public state line rather than a personal command transcript.
contrary_evidence: It shows restraint-oriented rhetoric, not a direct ruler command over external military force.
The source does not record private deliberation or internal dissent.

evidence.claim: Vietnam called on relevant sides to resume dialogue and address the Ukraine conflict through peaceful measures based on international law, and said it stood ready to contribute to dialogue and regional and global peace.
evidence.title: Viet Nam responds to Russian annexation of four Ukrainian regions
evidence.excerpt: Vietnam called on relevant sides to resume dialogue and address the Ukraine conflict through peaceful measures based on international law, and said it stood ready to contribute to dialogue and regional and global peace.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official response to Russia's annexation announcement, with dated and specific peace language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect to Trọng through the party-state foreign-policy line; still useful for the ruler-period external-security stance.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is declaratory diplomacy rather than a specific operational decision by Trọng.
It does not show how Vietnamese officials voted or negotiated internally.

evidence.claim: During Trọng's official visit to China, the two sides said issues at sea should be handled through peaceful means and international law, and that maintaining peace and stability in the East Sea is extremely important; they also pledged expanded diplomacy and security coordination.
evidence.title: Viet Nam, China issue joint statement
evidence.excerpt: During Trọng's official visit to China, the two sides said issues at sea should be handled through peaceful means and international law, and that maintaining peace and stability in the East Sea is extremely important; they also pledged expanded diplomacy and security coordination.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary text of the joint statement tied to a dated leader visit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct enough for Trọng's visit and resulting political guidance, though the text is still a bilateral party-state statement.
contrary_evidence: This is a negotiated diplomatic text, not evidence of a military de-escalation crisis or battlefield restraint decision.
It also reflects mutual Chinese interests, so not every clause is attributable solely to Trọng.

evidence.claim: RFA reported that Hanoi remained passive and gave no substantive comment beyond a formulaic call for restraint, while Vietnamese media covered the invasion with less of their usual pro-Russia bias than in 2014.
evidence.title: On Ukraine crisis, Vietnam media stray from typical pro-Russia coverage
evidence.excerpt: RFA reported that Hanoi remained passive and gave no substantive comment beyond a formulaic call for restraint, while Vietnamese media covered the invasion with less of their usual pro-Russia bias than in 2014.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent contemporaneous reporting, but explicitly analytical and not an official record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect to the Trọng-era party-state line; useful mainly as a counterpoint to the official restraint statements.
contrary_evidence: This is commentary-heavy reporting, so the diagnosis of passivity is interpretive rather than documentary.
It does not show Trọng personally directing the response.

evidence.claim: RFA said Trọng's visit was the first by a foreign leader since Xi's reelection and that analysts saw it as reinforcing close ties, with Vietnam having no intention to counter China by allying with a third nation.
evidence.title: Top Vietnamese leader heading to China on Sunday to meet Xi
evidence.excerpt: RFA said Trọng's visit was the first by a foreign leader since Xi's reelection and that analysts saw it as reinforcing close ties, with Vietnam having no intention to counter China by allying with a third nation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with explicit analyst attribution and contemporaneous timing, but the strategic conclusion is interpretive.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler-period context around the China visit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to the visit itself, but the 'no intention to counter China' point is analyst interpretation about Vietnam's strategy, not a quoted Trọng decision.
contrary_evidence: This can be read as strategic balancing rather than moral peacemaking.
The article does not show a concrete peace settlement or cessation action.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 ruler-attributed nuclear command, crisis, proliferation, or catastrophic dual-use decision is documented; the package relies on limited-exposure context and peace-oriented diplomacy.
No direct operational external-security, ceasefire-management, or war-fighting act by Trọng in 2022 is shown; the package is mostly declaratory diplomacy and restraint rhetoric.
The package does not show personally attributed incitement to communal violence or a clean ruler-led accountability reform that would offset the repression record.

Direct 2022 decision-path evidence is thin; the package leans on structural one-party baseline, media restrictions, and country reports rather than a direct record of Trọng personally directing repression.
Specific appointments of economic technocrats and household-level causal attribution remain indirect; most evidence is macro/system-level rather than personally executable by Trọng alone.
Service-delivery evidence is stronger than ruler attribution; subnational quality, regional inequality, and direct personal causal links remain thin.
There is no direct, independently verified evidence on Trọng's assets, gifts, family business interests, declaration filings, or other personal self-dealing records.
Personnel-selection evidence and direct causal attribution for program execution remain thinner than the program, implementation, and outcome record.
